title: Behavior Catalog PRD for Multi-Interface Hosted Inference + Launch Sanity Pack
creator: Ayesha Choudhury
description:
Problem: Product and platform teams need a single canonical source of truth describing expected runtime behavior across the four hosted inference surfaces (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). The goal of this PRD is to define a Behavior Catalog (canonical behavioral spec + deterministic acceptance criteria) that reduces ambiguity between SDKs, runtime routing, and customer-facing contracts, and to ship a Launch Sanity Pack that operationalizes tests and telemetry for go/no-go decisions.

Goals: Provide clear, machine-readable acceptance criteria and human-run sanity checks for each surface; codify common failure modes and graded degradations; include a lightweight canary test harness; and produce a launch checklist that the GTM/Support/Engineering teams can use for cutover.

Non-goals: This document does not redesign the underlying API shape, nor prescribe model-level evaluation datasets beyond linkage to the eval team. It also does not commit to per-tenant QoS profiles (that's a follow-up Dedicated capacity effort).
scope_changes: Initial scope: behavioral definitions + checklist for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank hosted surfaces.
Scope added 2025-02-18: include deterministic prefix-caching behavior expectations for streamed chat responses (requested by Runtime team).
Scope removed 2025-02-22: dropped long-term telemetry retention policy (moved to Observability product ticket).
requirements_clarifications: API contract: this PRD assumes existing endpoint payloads remain unchanged; behavioral expectations are layered on top of current contract headers and response codes.

Latency SLOs: default lane SLOs are 95th percentile <= 180ms per token for short-sequence completions (<=128 tokens), and <= 350ms for chat streaming first-byte across common models. Exact numbers are advisory — engineering to validate via benchmark harness.

Determinism: rerank endpoint must be stable for identical inputs and model version pinned; minor nondeterminism due to model backs (float16 kernels) is acceptable if variance is documented under "graded degradation".
Fallbacks: behavior catalog must enumerate compatible fallback model variants and expected quality delta (high/medium/low) for each official lane.
Schema: acceptance criteria must be expressible as boolean / threshold checks in the Launch Sanity Pack harness (see testing_plan links).
acceptance_criteria: API conformance: example request/response for each surface passes schema validators and sample golden responses match within tolerated diffs for 95% of cases.
Latency: end-to-end synthetic traffic for the targeted lane meets SLOs on dedicated test cluster for 2 consecutive days under 70% of target TPS.
Correctness: embeddings cosine similarity between current and canary models within configured delta for 90% of golden prompt set.
Rerank stability: top-5 ranking intersection between baseline and canary >= 0.85 on rerank acceptance set.
Streaming integrity: streamed chat responses must contain ordered chunking with incremental token offsets and no duplicate tokens across chunks for 99.9% of sessions in canary traffic.
Graceful degradation: automatic fallback invoked and success rate restored above 95% when simulated model variant is taken offline (failover test).
Operational: alert rules (latency, error rate, token inflation) fire in the intended on-call path and paging playbook has been validated in a simulated incident run.
launch_checklist: PRD sign-off by Product, Runtime Eng, Observability, and Security (signatures in Confluence comments).
Sanity Pack deployed to canary cluster and run against canary traffic slice (2% of production) for 72 hours.
All failing checks in Sanity Pack triaged and either fixed or accepted with documented risk and rollback plan.
Client SDK compatibility smoke tests passed for JS/Python and backward-compatibility notes published.
Runbook published with step-by-step rollback: toggle routing to previous model lane, invalidate KV prefix cache if needed, and target autoscaling adjustments.
Support-run checklist: customer-facing FAQ draft, known-issues table, escalation matrix, and sample curl/SDK commands for verification.
Security review completed and required KMS/HSM notes present for Private/Dedicated lanes.
Telemetry dashboards: per-route latency, cost-per-token, quality-regression gauges, and consumer-visibility links created and reviewed.
Legal / compliance: data retention brief completed for hosted lanes and exceptions documented.
rollout_strategy: Phase 0 - Internal Canary: deploy to internal cluster, synthetic and internal user tests for 72 hours.
Phase 1 - Gradual Canary (2%): route 2% of production traffic for 7 days; run automated Sanity Pack continuously and manual sample audits daily.
Phase 2 - Broad Canary (15%): increase to 15% if Phase 1 stable for 72 hours; validate customer interaction telemetry and billing/usage alignment.
Phase 3 - GA Cutover: ladder rollout in regions with fallback routing and post-cutover monitoring for 48 hours at each increment.
Rollback triggers: sustained error rate >1.5% OR latency SLO breaches for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows OR quality regressions on eval set beyond threshold.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: streaming chunk ordering regressions after kernel optimizations. Mitigation: add chunk-ordering unit tests and end-to-end fuzz harness; block launch until failure rate <0.1%.
Risk: rerank stability anomalies due to quantization changes. Mitigation: require model variant compatibility matrix and per-tenant pilot for customers with strict ranking SLAs.
Risk: telemetry blind spots for multi-tenant lanes. Mitigation: enforce token-level tagging in requests during canary and validate dashboards read that tag.
Risk: unexpected cost amplification from batching heuristics. Mitigation: simulate cost under representative latency-limited workloads and cap burst autoscaling during canary.
decisions: 2025-02-16: Keep API schemas unchanged; behavior catalog is orthogonal and enforced via Sanity Pack checks.
2025-02-19: Include prefix/KV caching expectations for streaming chat (accepted).
2025-02-25: Require Security review prior to GA for hosted lanes (accepted).
testing_plan: Sanity Pack (automated): schema validators, synthetic traffic latency and error checks, embedding similarity checks, rerank intersection metrics, and streaming chunk integrity tests.
Manual audits: daily human review of 200 sampled chat sessions in canary and annotation for hallucination/regression flags.
Load tests: run bench harness at 120% of expected production TPS to validate autoscaling policies and cost knobs.
Chaos test: simulate model host loss and verify fallback logic and KV invalidation behave as expected.
SDK tests: cross-version compatibility tests for JS/Python and basic example apps in the sandbox org.
telemetry_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-surface KPI board (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, embedding drift index, rerank stability score).
Alerts: page on error rate > 1.5% sustained for 10 minutes, page on latency SLO breach at p95 for 3 consecutive 5m windows.
Quality regression monitors: automated daily eval runs with alert to product when quality delta exceeds threshold.
Tagging: add token-level "canary-v" header for traffic slicing and billing reconciliation during rollout.
